{{Nihongo|'''Hidetoshi Nakata''', <small>[[Order of the Star of Italian Solidarity|OSSI]]</small>|中田 英寿|Nakata Hidetoshi|born 22 January 1977}} is a Japanese former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]]. Considered as one of the greatest Asian football players of all time and coming from an [[Asian Football Confederation]] (AFC) country in the late 1990s and early 2000s,<ref name="CNN">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37410597/the-best-asian-players-all?platform=amp|title=Countdown: The Top 10 Asian footballers of all time|author=Duerden, John|date=7 June 2015|website=ESPN|access-date=28 August 2023|archive-date=28 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230828154722/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37410597/the-best-asian-players-all?platform=amp|url-status=live}}</ref> Nakata became the first ever AFC player to be nominated for the [[Ballon d'Or]]. 

Nakata began his professional career in 1995 and won the [[Asian Football Confederation]] Player of the Year award in 1997 and 1998, the [[Scudetto]] with [[AS Roma|Roma]] in 2001, played for [[Japan national football team|Japan]] in three [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] tournaments ([[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]], [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002]] and [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006]]) and competed in the [[Football at the Summer Olympics|Olympics]] twice ([[Football at the 1996 Summer Olympics|1996]] and [[Football at the 2000 Summer Olympics|2000]]).<ref>{{cite Sports-Reference}}</ref> In 2005, he was made the [[Order of the Star of Italian Solidarity|Knight of the Order of the Star of Italian Solidarity]], one of Italy's highest honors, for improving the country's image overseas.<ref name="nakata_knight">{{cite news|title=Arise, Sir Nak! |url=http://archive.thisislancashire.co.uk/2005/10/14/872606.html |publisher=This Is Lancashire |date=14 October 2005 |access-date=3 July 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090214230937/http://archive.thisislancashire.co.uk/2005/10/14/872606.html |archive-date=14 February 2009 }}</ref> Nakata has also been involved in fashion, regularly attending runway shows and wearing designer clothing.

Nakata announced his retirement at the age of 29 on 3 July 2006, after a ten-year career that included seven seasons in the Italian [[Serie A]] and a season in the English [[Premier League]]. In March 2004, [[Pelé]] named Nakata in his [[FIFA 100]], a list of the top living footballers at the time. Nakata was one of only two Asian footballers on the list.

==Club career==

===Bellmare===
Nakata began his professional career at the age of 18 in 1995, with [[J1 League]] side [[Shonan Bellmare|Bellmare Hiratsuka]] (now [[Shonan Bellmare]]). He played many matches as an attacking midfielder in his first season and the club won the [[1995 Asian Cup Winners' Cup]], the first Asian title in the club's history. In the final against [[Al-Talaba SC|Al-Talaba]], he scored the winning goal in the 81st minute.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/ascup96.html |title=RSSSF |access-date=2 February 2023 |archive-date=5 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405000420/https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/ascup96.html |url-status=live }}</ref> From 1996, he was a regular player and he was selected for the [[J.League Best XI]] in 1997. 

===Perugia===
After the 1998 World Cup in France, Nakata was signed by [[AC Perugia Calcio|Perugia]] in Italy's [[Serie A]] for 4 million [[United States dollar|U.S. dollars]],<ref>{{cite news |author=Paddy Agnew |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/jul/24/newsstory.sport1 |title=The Hidetoshi Nakata story in Serie A &#124; Football |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=25 September 2016 |archive-date=9 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309144851/http://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/jul/24/newsstory.sport1 |url-status=live }}</ref> becoming the second Japanese player ever to appear in the Italian top league after [[Kazuyoshi Miura]] had done it for [[Genoa CFC|Genoa]] four years earlier. Scepticism initially surrounded his arrival, but Nakata quickly established himself as a sensation in Italian football, scoring a brace on his debut against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in a 3–4 defeat.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/1998/settembre/19/Nakata_samurai_regna_Perugia_co_0_98091912418.shtml |title=Nakata, un samurai regna a Perugia |newspaper=[[Corriere della Sera]] |author=Goffredo Buccini |date=19 September 1998 |page=16 |language=it}}</ref> 

Operating primarily as an attacking midfielder, Nakata was known for his vision, passing range, and ability to contribute offensively with late runs and shots from distance. His technical skill was demonstrated early in his spell at the club by a notable acrobatic volley in a 2–0 win over Piacenza.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.ilgiornale.it/news/calcio/perugia-provincia-giappone-quando-gaucci-port-nakata-2376609.html |title=Perugia, provincia del Giappone: quando Gaucci portò Nakata |newspaper=[[Il Giornale]] |author=Paolo Lazzari |date=5 October 2024 |language=it }}</ref> Beyond his performances on the pitch, his transfer generated widespread attention, leading thousands of Japanese fans and specialized tour operators to travel to Umbria to watch matches at the [[Stadio Renato Curi]], while also resulting in significant merchandise sales in Japan.<ref>{{cite news |author=Paddy Agnew |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/jul/24/newsstory.sport1 |title=The Hidetoshi Nakata story in Serie A &#124; Football |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=25 September 2016 |archive-date=9 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309144851/http://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/jul/24/newsstory.sport1 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In his first season with the *Grifoni*, he played 32 matches and scored 10 goals—his single-season highest total—helping the club secure safety in Serie A.<ref>{{cite news |lang=en |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/11/30/sports/30iht-nakata.t.html |title=Nakata, 21, Lifts Perugia and Ranks 5th on League Scoring Chart: Italy's Japanese Soccer Sensation |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |author=Paddy Agnew |date=30 November 1998 }}</ref> He continued to feature prominently into the following campaign, making 15 league appearances and scoring 2 goals before transferring midway through the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www2.raisport.rai.it/news/rubriche/cmercato/200001/13/387e10e200f7f/|title=Nakata è della Roma|date=13 January 2000|language=it|access-date=13 May 2014|archive-date=14 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514232243/http://www2.raisport.rai.it/news/rubriche/cmercato/200001/13/387e10e200f7f/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Roma===
In January 2000, Nakata moved to [[AS Roma|Roma]] for 42 billion [[Italian lira|lire]], helping the team win the [[scudetto]].<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.borsaitaliana.it/bitApp/view.bit?lang=it&target=DocViewerDownload&filename=db%2Fpdf%2F1094.pdf| title = BILANCIO D'ESERCIZIO E CONSOLIDATO DI GRUPPO AL 30 GIUGNO 2000| date = 28 June 2001| language = it| access-date = 24 March 2015| work = AS Roma| publisher = Borsa Italiana Archive| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20161221001137/http://www.borsaitaliana.it/bitApp/view.bit?lang=it&target=DocViewerDownload&filename=db%2Fpdf%2F1094.pdf| archive-date = 21 December 2016| url-status = dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/serie-a/fotogallery/2017/06/17/accadde-oggi-la-roma-vince-terzo-scudetto.html |title=17 giugno 2001: e Roma impazzì per lo scudetto |publisher=sport.sky.it |language=it |date=17 June 2017 |access-date=11 October 2019 |archive-date=11 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191011013504/https://sport.sky.it/calcio/serie-a/fotogallery/2017/06/17/accadde-oggi-la-roma-vince-terzo-scudetto.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.borsaitaliana.it/bitApp/view.bit?lang=it&target=DocViewerDownload&filename=db%2Fpdf%2F1094.pdf| title = BILANCIO D'ESERCIZIO E CONSOLIDATO DI GRUPPO AL 30 GIUGNO 2000| date = 28 June 2001| language = it| access-date = 24 March 2015| work = AS Roma| publisher = Borsa Italiana Archive| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20161221001137/http://www.borsaitaliana.it/bitApp/view.bit?lang=it&target=DocViewerDownload&filename=db%2Fpdf%2F1094.pdf| archive-date = 21 December 2016| url-status = dead}}</ref> The highlight of Nakata's career at Roma came on 6 May 2001 in a Serie A match against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] at [[Stadio Delle Alpi]]. After replacing [[Francesco Totti]] in the second half with Roma trailing 0–2, Nakata netted with a 30-yard goal beyond Juventus [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] [[Edwin van der Sar]]'s reach, with 11 minutes left in the match. He then helped Roma score the equalizer when his fierce drive from outside the box was parried by Van der Sar into the path of [[Vincenzo Montella]], who scored for Roma in the last minute. The match ended with a 2–2 draw and Roma maintained a six-point margin at the top of the league table.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.repubblica.it/online/campionato_partite/juveroma/juveroma/juveroma.html |title=la Repubblica/campionato_partite: Montella e Nakata rimontano la Juve |website=Repubblica.it |access-date=25 September 2016 |archive-date=2 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171002220336/http://www.repubblica.it/online/campionato_partite/juveroma/juveroma/juveroma.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

date =6 July 2001| access-date =5 January 2013| publisher =BBC| archive-date =6 October 2014| archive-url Asian player which would not be broken for 14 years.<ref>{{cite book|title=AS Roma SpA bilancio 30.06.2001|trans-title=AS Roma SpA Report and Accounts on 30 June 2001|publisher=CCIAA] (Italian company ===Later years===
In January 2004, Nakata played for [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]] where he played the remainder of the 2003–04 season before moving to [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]], where he played the following season. In August 2005, Nakata moved to [[FA Premier League|Premiership]] side [[Bolton Wanderers]] on loan. During his season at Bolton, which would be the last of his professional career, he scored once in the league, in a 2–0 win over [[West Bromwich Albion]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Bolton 2-0 West Brom|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/4344558.stm|publisher=BBC|date=23 October 2005|access-date=15 September 2009|archive-date=13 November 2005|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051113031912/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/4344558.stm|url-status=live}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Hidetoshi Nakata, preparing for Football World Cup 2006.jpg|thumb|right|Nakata training with Japan at the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]]]]
After having represented [[Japan national under-17 football team|U-17 Japan]] at the [[1993 FIFA U-17 World Championship|1993 U-17 World Championship]] (where he scored a goal) and [[Japan national under-20 football team|U-20 Japan]] at the [[1995 FIFA World Youth Championship|1995 U-20 World Championship]] (where he scored twice), Nakata was part of the [[Japan national under-23 football team|U-23 Japan]] squads at the [[Football at the 1996 Summer Olympics|1996 Olympics]], where Japan upset [[Brazil national under-23 football team|Brazil]],<ref name="FIFAwc_miracle">{{cite news|title=Japan in need of miracle|url=http://fifaworldcup.yahoo.com/06/en/060621/1/80s3.html|publisher=[[2006 FIFA World Cup]]|date=21 June 2006|access-date=3 July 2006}}</ref> and at the [[Football at the 2000 Summer Olympics|2000 Olympics]]. His [[Japan national football team|senior national team]] debut came in May 1997 against [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]].<ref name=nationalteam>{{cite web| url =http://www.jfootball-db.com/en/players/nakata_hidetoshi.html| title =NAKATA Hidetoshi| publisher =Japan National Football Team Database| url-status =dead| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20130515183301/http://www.japannationalfootballteam.com/en/players/nakata_hidetoshi.html| archive-date =15 May 2013}}</ref>

He was a key member of the Japanese side that qualified for the [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998 World Cup]], scoring five goals in qualification matches and setting up all three Japanese goals in the [[1998 FIFA World Cup qualification (AFC)#Play-off|qualification play-off]] against [[Iran national football team|Iran]]. He helped Japan reach the final of the [[2001 FIFA Confederations Cup|2001 Confederations Cup]] but left the national team before the final to join Roma for their final league matches.<ref name="AP_confedcup">{{cite magazine|title=Just making the final was a triumph for cup co-host|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/news/2001/06/11/japan_confed/|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|agency=Associated Press|date=11 June 2001|access-date=3 July 2006|archive-date=20 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020044227/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/news/2001/06/11/japan_confed/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Nakata played in all four of Japan's matches at the [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002 World Cup]], co-hosted by [[South Korea]] and Japan, scoring the second goal of a 2–0 first round win against [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]].

At the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]], Nakata played in all three matches for Japan, losing to [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] and [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]], and drawing with [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]]. His performance against Croatia earned him a Man of the Match award.<ref>{{cite news|title=Japan 0-0 Croatia|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4853196.stm|work=BBC News|date=18 June 2006|access-date=7 July 2008|archive-date=19 June 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060619111359/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4853196.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> After the 2006 FIFA World Cup, on 3 July 2006, Nakata announced his retirement from professional football and the Japanese national team on his personal website "I decided half a year ago that I would retire from the world of professional football&nbsp;... after the World Cup in Germany." Nakata wrote, "I will never again stand on the pitch as a professional player. But I will never give up football."<ref name="reuters_retirement">{{cite news|title=Japan and Bolton midfielder Nakata to retire|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=373155&cc=5901|agency=[[Reuters]]|date=3 July 2006|access-date=3 July 2006|archive-date=24 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120224204836/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=373155&cc=5901|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=To live is to journey, and to journey is to live. |url=http://www.nakata.net/en/hidesmail/hml16700.htm |publisher=Hidetoshi Nakata |date=3 July 2006 |access-date=22 January 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070517230107/http://www.nakata.net/en/hidesmail/hml16700.htm |archive-date=17 May 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In a 2014 interview in ''TMW Magazine'', Nakata confirmed that he had retired at such a young age because he was no longer enjoying football, and wanted instead to see what was going on in the world.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Guerri |first=Cristina |date=January 2014 |title=In viaggio con Nakata |trans-title=On the road with Nakata |url=http://www.tmwmagazine.com/download/?id=MDQxLXBkZi1sbw&source=web-tmwmagazine |language=it |magazine=TMW Magazine |page=10 |access-date=1 September 2014 |quote=Hidetoshi Nakata ha scelto di appendere le scarpette al chiodo ancora giovanissimo. "Il motivo? Non mi divertivo più. Ho preferito scoprire cosa c'è nel mondo, e devo dire che ho imparato molto". (Hidetoshi Nakata chose to hang up his boots while still very young. "The reason? I wasn't enjoying it any more. I preferred to find out what was going on in the world, and I must say I learnt a lot". |archive-date=3 April 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140403194213/http://www.tmwmagazine.com/download/?id=MDQxLXBkZi1sbw&source=web-tmwmagazine |url-status=live }}</ref>

Despite Nakata playing every match in Japan's first three World Cup appearances, he was not selected for the country's [[AFC Asian Cup|Asian Cup]]-winning squads in [[2000 AFC Asian Cup|2000]] and [[2004 AFC Asian Cup|2004]]. In total, he was capped 77 times for Japan, scoring 11 goals, 9 of which came in official FIFA competitions.<ref name=nationalteam/>

==Style of play==
A quick, creative, and hard-working [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking]] or [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|central midfielder]], with an eye for goal, Nakata was known for his technical ability, agility, vision, passing, and his ability to make attacking runs into the penalty area and score goals; he also possessed a powerful shot from outside the box.<ref name="CNN"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.footballmagazineitalia.it/index.php/archivio/ultime-notizie/99-dal-giappone-con-furore|title=Dal Giappone con furore|trans-title=From Japan, with furor|publisher=Football Magazine Italia|language=it|date=13 May 2014|access-date=1 October 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304044353/http://www.footballmagazineitalia.it/index.php/archivio/ultime-notizie/99-dal-giappone-con-furore|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://sport.repubblica.it/news/sport/calcio-bologna-signori-nakata-ci-dara-quel/395997?refresh_ce|title=Calcio, Bologna; Signori: Nakata ci darà quel che ci manca|trans-title=Football, Bologna; Signori: Nakata will give us what we are missing|newspaper=La Repubblica|language=it|access-date=1 October 2015|archive-date=7 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107025600/http://sport.repubblica.it/news/sport/calcio-bologna-signori-nakata-ci-dara-quel/395997?refresh_ce|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/2211310/nakata-returning-to-roma|title=NAKATA RETURNING TO ROMA|publisher=www.skysports.com|author1=James Burton|access-date=3 November 2017|archive-date=3 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180803000417/http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/2211310/nakata-returning-to-roma|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/it/notizie/nakata-lantidivo-che-e-entrato-nella-storia-della-roma-quasi-senza-rendersene-conto/1trgymxbimza21jcs85uv4r1sg |title=Nakata, l'antidivo che è entrato nella storia della Roma quasi senza rendersene conto |publisher=www.goal.com |language=it |date=22 January 2023 |access-date=17 January 2024 |archive-date=26 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230526155026/https://www.goal.com/it/notizie/nakata-lantidivo-che-e-entrato-nella-storia-della-roma-quasi-senza-rendersene-conto/1trgymxbimza21jcs85uv4r1sg |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Outside football==
Outside football, Nakata has shown interest in fashion, attending runway shows, wearing designer clothing and sporting colorful haircuts. He dyed his hair blond for the [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998 World Cup]], hoping to attract the attention of European scouts. Japanese hairstylist Aki Watanabe credits him as a trendsetter.<ref name="bbc_hair">{{cite news|first=Efe|last=Sodje|title=Footballers&nbsp;... haircuts. Not always the best combination!|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/england/stoke_and_staffordshire|publisher=BBC|year=2002|access-date=4 July 2006|archive-date=6 April 2005|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050406005954/http://www.bbc.co.uk/stoke/sport/2003/10/worldcup_haircuts.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> Andrea Tenerani, photographer for ''[[GQ (magazine)|GQ]]'' in Italy said of Nakata, "He's perfect; he's like a model. And he's totally obsessed with fashion."<ref name="iht_fashion">{{cite news|first=J. J. |last=Martin |title=Feast for marketers: It's all about soccer |url=http://www.iht.com/articles/2004/07/01/rsoccer_ed3_.php |work=[[International Herald Tribune]] |date=1 July 2002 |access-date=4 July 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060827080329/http://www.iht.com/articles/2004/07/01/rsoccer_ed3_.php |archive-date=27 August 2006 |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Calvin Klein]] designer [[Italo Zucchelli]] said, "(Nakata) plays with fashion like all of them now, but in a cooler, more sophisticated way than many others."<ref name="nyt_fashion">{{cite news|first=Eric |last=Wilson |title=BLEACH IT LIKE BECKHAM: World Cup of hair style |url=http://www.charlotte.com/mld/charlotte/living/style/14880165.htm |newspaper=New York Times |date=22 June 2006 |access-date=4 July 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060716031632/http://www.charlotte.com/mld/charlotte/living/style/14880165.htm |archive-date=16 July 2006 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is one of the models featuring the [[Calvin Klein]] underwear campaign 2010. He was featured in the July 2007 US version of ''[[GQ (magazine)|GQ]]'' with a 12-page spread on fall fashion. He was featured in ''[[GQ (magazine)|GQ]]'' in his home country in December 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://storemags.com/gq-december-2011-japan/ |title=GQ – December 2011 Japan free download in PDF |website=Storemags.com |access-date=25 September 2016 |archive-date=27 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160927060457/http://storemags.com/gq-december-2011-japan/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
[[File:サッカー元日本代表 (30907917805).jpg|thumb|right|Nakata (middle) at a fashion event in Tokyo, November 2016]]
Often regarded as a Japanese [[David Beckham]],<ref>[https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/news/newsid=1436739.html] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110918211015/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/news/newsid%3D1436739.html|date=18 September 2011}}</ref> Nakata is an editor-at-large at ''[[Monocle (2007 magazine)|Monocle]]'' magazine at the invitation of his friend [[Tyler Brûlé]], who serves as the magazine's editor-in-chief.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nakata.net/jp/chaser/chs67100.htm |title=Hide Chaser ｜nakata.net -- 中田英寿オフィシャルホームページ |access-date=12 June 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080820061245/http://nakata.net/jp/chaser/chs67100.htm |archive-date=20 August 2008 }}</ref> Nakata has cited the popular [[manga]] and [[anime]] series, ''[[Captain Tsubasa]]'', as his primary inspiration in choosing football as a career.<ref>''[https://web.archive.org/web/20140201234519/http://www.thesundaytimes.co.uk/sto/sport/football/article210278.ece 'I don't understand why people are football fans. I don't like to watch any kind of sport']'' - by Jonathan Northcroft, ''[[The Sunday Times (UK)|The Sunday Times]]'', 1 January 2006.</ref> In recent years, he has also been an active supporter of Special Olympics football and participated in the 2010 Special Olympics Unity Cup<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.specialolympicsnig.org/unified_sports.html |title=Special Olympics Nigeria - Initiatives - Unified Sports |access-date=15 December 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141215234516/http://www.specialolympicsnig.org/unified_sports.html |archive-date=15 December 2014 }}</ref> in South Africa during the World Cup. Nakata was named a Global Ambassador for Special Olympics in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.specialolympics.org/Press/2014/Nakata_Named_Global_Ambassador.aspx |title=Special Olympics: Nakata Named Global Ambassador |access-date=15 December 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150325223300/http://specialolympics.org/Press/2014/Nakata_Named_Global_Ambassador.aspx |archive-date=25 March 2015 }}</ref>

Towards the end of 2015, Nakata entered into a partnership with Kee Club in [[Hong Kong]] to open Koko, a Hong Kong-based restaurant that serves sakes created by Nakata himself. He has developed his own line of sake as well as creating his own mobile educational app, "Sakenomy". Expressing interest in educating the public about sake, Nakata stated, "People recognise brands of wine but not usually brands of sake. There is a lack of information and branding when it comes to sake. That’s why I thought I needed to create a brand that people can recognise and understand. My purpose is to expand the market for all sake not just my own. You can pair any type of cuisine with sake. It can go with French, Italian, even Chinese food, not just Japanese cuisine."<ref>{{cite web|title=Q&A: Hidetoshi Nakata on his new Wyndham Street izakaya, Koko|url=http://www.timeout.com.hk/restaurants-bars/features/75201/qa-hidetoshi-nakata-on-his-new-wyndham-street-izakaya-koko.html|website=Time Out Hong Kong|access-date=31 December 2015|archive-date=4 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160104183610/http://www.timeout.com.hk/restaurants-bars/features/75201/qa-hidetoshi-nakata-on-his-new-wyndham-street-izakaya-koko.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Media===
Having been signed to sportswear company [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]], Nakata featured in Nike's "[[Secret Tournament]]" advertisement (branded "Scorpion KO") directed by [[Terry Gilliam]], in the buildup to the 2002 World Cup in Korea and Japan.<ref name="Nike"/> He appeared alongside other star football players from around the world, including [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]], [[Ronaldinho]], [[Luís Figo]], [[Thierry Henry]], [[Roberto Carlos (footballer)|Roberto Carlos]] and [[Francesco Totti]], with former player [[Eric Cantona]] the tournament "referee".<ref name="Nike">{{cite news |title=A lighter shoe, cooler kits, a faster ball, a Secret Tournament – every touch counts |url=http://www.nikebiz.com/story/stry_scorpion.shtml |work=NikeBiz |publisher=Nike |access-date=16 February 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020602055510/http://www.nikebiz.com/story/stry_scorpion.shtml |archive-date=2 June 2002 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Claire |last=Cozens |title=Cantona hosts World Cup with a difference |url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2002/apr/03/advertising.worldcupfootball2002?INTCMP=ILCNETTXT3487 |work=The Guardian |publisher=Guardian News and Media |date=3 April 2002 |access-date=16 February 2015 |archive-date=1 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180701165023/https://www.theguardian.com/media/2002/apr/03/advertising.worldcupfootball2002?INTCMP=ILCNETTXT3487 |url-status=live }}</ref> Nakata featured on the front cover of various Japanese editions of [[EA Sports]]’ [[FIFA (video game series)|''FIFA'' video game series]], including ''[[FIFA Football 2002]]''. In 2018, Nakata was added as an icon to the Ultimate Team in ''[[FIFA 19]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=FIFA 19 Ultimate Team: What Icons are in the new game and how do you get them? |url=http://www.goal.com/en-ie/news/fifa-19-ultimate-team-what-icons-are-in-the-new-game-and-how/1qrv1f9kllmhd12ffdqdmfy91j |access-date=12 September 2018 |agency=Goal |archive-date=12 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180912131333/http://www.goal.com/en-ie/news/fifa-19-ultimate-team-what-icons-are-in-the-new-game-and-how/1qrv1f9kllmhd12ffdqdmfy91j |url-status=live }}</ref>
In the 2012 video game [[Inazuma Eleven 2|''Inazuma Eleven 2: Firestorm / Blizzard'']] Nakata was added as a hidden playable player. He then served an important story role in ''[[Inazuma Eleven 3]]'' and its respective anime series, where Nakata would serve as the captain of the Italian team Orpheus.
